tasks.short: Read books aloud to preschool groups

steps.what: Read books to entire classes or small groups and respond to children's participation

tasks.design: Keep shared reading live with the teacher. Existing book choices may sit in {DOCS}, but an audio recording does not replace responding to the children during reading.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is shared attention and interaction, not text production.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is needed for the unchanged activity.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting pace, voice and questions to different children.
tasks.human_edge: Notice who wants to join in and make space for their response.
tasks.altitude: Reading time and teaching authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Support a child joining a small-group reading session
reach.learn: Shared reading routines and inclusive participation

evidence.claim: Live shared reading includes responsive interaction that a generated reading artefact does not replace.

assumptions: Boundary is live reading after book selection, not lesson planning or library acquisition.
Children's responses are heard in s1 with full teacher time retained; no structured engagement or emotion data is captured.
Native software is unnecessary for this activity. Zero incremental upkeep because no new automation, content bank or data collection is added.
unknowns: Typical group size and language needs
research_questions: Which reading moments depend most on a teacher responding to the group?

already_counted.description: Read aloud and respond to children

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. All live reading and interaction remain; no saving from replacing teacher presence is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish learning objectives and explain them to children

steps.what: Choose appropriate lesson, unit and project objectives from curriculum goals
Write clear objectives for lessons, units and projects
Check objective meaning, developmental suitability and correspondence to the planned activity
Communicate the objectives to children using examples and accessible language

tasks.design: Configure a small bank of teacher-approved objective wording in {DOCS}, selected by curriculum goal and activity. Reuse text where it fits, retain manual writing for new objectives, and keep teacher checking and explanation to children intact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated objective wording takes time, while choosing a suitable learning purpose remains a teaching decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document templates and goal-linked sections can reuse established wording without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the objective is meaningful and achievable for this group.
tasks.human_edge: Translate a learning purpose into something young children can understand and experience.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated writing; goal selection and teaching rights do not change.

reach.task: Compare a planned activity with its stated curriculum objective
reach.learn: Goal progression and developmentally suitable language

evidence.claim: Reusable goal-linked text can reduce repeated objective writing while a teacher retains selection and review.
An NFER/EEF trial of secondary science planning found reduced preparation time with guided AI use; it does not measure preschool objective writing or validate this saving estimate.

assumptions: Boundary is selecting, documenting, checking and communicating objectives, not creating the full lesson or assessing individual children. Shared lesson-planning time must be allocated once in roll-ups.

Teacher produces goal code, activity, group age range and intended learning in s1, retaining 30 hours. Curriculum coordinator already maintains the curriculum goal list outside this task; no new child profile is inferred.
Teacher chooses and adapts existing wording in s2's retained 15 hours. The teacher produces any new wording manually; ongoing additions and revisions cost the incremental hour below.
Missing or unsuitable bank entries trigger manual writing. Test native templates before custom code; no automated learning-outcome judgement or pupil scoring is introduced.
s3 approves the complete objective revision before s4 explains it; changed text returns to review.
unknowns: How often activities require new objectives
research_questions: Does reused wording fit the activity and remain clear when explained to children?

already_counted.description: Select goals, adapt wording, check suitability and explain objectives

incremental.description: Maintain goal links and revise reusable objective wording

approvals.approved_version: Completed objective text linked to goal and planned activity; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+15+15+25=85; gross 15 minus upkeep 1 gives net 14. E1 scenario halves wording time for recurring objectives only. Novel activities and unsuitable bank text may leave no net gain; explanation time never falls.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach eating habits and personal hygiene

steps.what: Teach proper eating habits and personal hygiene by explaining and modelling routines
Guide children practising eating and hygiene routines and respond to difficulties

tasks.design: Keep modelling and supported practice with the teacher. Existing routine guidance in {DOCS} can remain available, without replacing the adult who notices difficulties and helps the child.
tasks.previous_blocker: Children learn these habits through repeated supported action, not just instructions.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional software is necessary for the unchanged routine.
tasks.still_hard: Different motor skills, sensory preferences and support needs.
tasks.human_edge: Offer patient assistance while respecting a child's dignity.
tasks.altitude: No reduction in time helping children or change in care responsibilities.

reach.task: Support a child practising a hygiene routine
reach.learn: Consistent prompts and individual support arrangements

evidence.claim: Teaching daily habits involves live modelling and responsive support that remain human in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is teaching and guided practice, not food preparation, clinical dietary advice or facility cleaning.
Teacher observes children's needs and practice within the retained steps; no structured compliance flag, image analysis or new record is introduced.
No generated medical or hygiene advice is proposed. Native document access is sufficient and requires no build.
Zero incremental upkeep because the existing routines and guidance remain unchanged.
research_questions: Where do children need direct assistance rather than an additional instructional artefact?

already_counted.description: Model habits and support children's practice

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net zero. Retain modelling, supervision and individual assistance rather than assume instructions shorten practice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Demonstrate activities to children, adjusting pace and technique to their responses

tasks.design: Retain the live demonstration and adaptation with the teacher. Planning materials in {DOCS} remain support for the activity, without substituting a generated presentation for teacher presence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Showing a technique includes physical modelling and immediate adjustment.
tasks.enabler_now: No technology change is needed for this live teaching step.
tasks.still_hard: Helping children with different attention, language and motor skills follow the activity safely.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion and show the activity another way.
tasks.altitude: Demonstration time and responsibility do not change.

reach.task: Reinforce a demonstrated activity with a small group
reach.learn: Safe materials and alternative ways to model the technique

evidence.claim: Live demonstrations require physical modelling and responses to children's understanding; this is not replaced by generating an artefact.

assumptions: Boundary is the live demonstration, after lesson planning and material preparation. Overlap with reading or hygiene demonstrations must be allocated once in a roll-up.
Teacher observes responses during s1 with all time retained. No structured ability score or emotion inference is used.
Check existing materials before adding software; no new software is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new content, data collection or automation is introduced.
unknowns: Activities and materials used most often
research_questions: Which activities require the teacher to change a demonstration in response to the group?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Retain all live modelling and adaptation; planning artefacts are outside this task's saving boundary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher spends less time repeating objective wording while retaining live reading, care routines and demonstrations.
reach: Help instructional coordination check activity-to-goal alignment
Guide assistants in inclusive small-group routines
role.ambitious_version: A preschool teacher with clearer activity objectives and the same time and attention available for children.
